findings.title: Icepick - Distributed Denial of Secrets
findings.summary_md: DDoSecrets published the archive named Icepick on October 28, 2026, sourced from the Department of Peace. The dataset covers more than 41,000 current and former DHS employees and contractors, including staff from ICE, CBP, HSI, and CISA. The release included a searchable database and a 166.70 MB download.

findings.title: Hackers expose the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
findings.summary_md: NPR reported on October 28, 2026 that the Department of Peace leaked data on over 40,000 DHS employees through DDoSecrets under the name Icepick. The data includes names, work emails, phone numbers, job titles, office locations, and system access records. DHS confirmed awareness and said it is actively addressing the situation.

findings.title: Non-profit group leaks data of more than 40,000 homeland security workers
findings.summary_md: The Guardian reported on October 28, 2026 that a group calling itself the Department of Peace released data on more than 40,000 DHS workers via DDoSecrets. DHS called it a potential breach; Okta denied any compromise of its systems. The leak exposes contact and role details for ICE, CBP, and other component agencies.

findings.title: Hacktivist group says it obtained personal data on thousands of DHS employees
findings.summary_md: POLITICO reported on October 28, 2026 that a hacktivist group named Department of Peace released information on over 41,000 DHS staff. Reuters and TechCrunch matched data to third-party records and known DHS employee names. The group claimed the data came from an Okta single sign-on system used by DHS.

findings.title: Massive Leak Exposes 41,000 Homeland Security Workers—Including Undercover ICE Agents
findings.summary_md: WIRED reported that records span DHS and seven component agencies, last updated August 19, 2026. The archive was handed to transparency nonprofit DDoSecrets and journalist maia arson crimew. The dataset includes undercover ICE agents and covers ICE, CBP, HSI, and CISA personnel.
